ir_definition: number of data samples in the majority class over the number of data samples in the minority class, for both binary and multi-class datasets

chosen.classifier: SVM (simple SVM for binary; multi-class SVM one-vs-rest for multi-class)
chosen.condition: original data, no added noise; 80:20 train/test split, 5 runs averaged, default parameters

rows.best_other_name: SMOTE (highest among the six compared methods)
SMOTE (highest among the six compared methods)

summary_rows.label: Wilcoxon CBHSID vs SMOTE G-mean (Table 8c, p.12)

outcome.stat_test: Friedman test (alpha 0.05) with Bonferroni-Dunn post-hoc (CD=2.014, Fig. 4) and Wilcoxon signed-ranks (Table 8). G-mean: CBHSID vs SMOTE significant in both Bonferroni-Dunn text (p.11) and Wilcoxon p=.02 **; Recall and F1 vs SMOTE not significant (p=.109, p=.066).

win_claim.quote: Based on Geometric-Mean (G-Mean), Recall, and F1-score, our method outperformed the other compared methods on 14 datasets out of 16.

uncertain: Table 3 prints 'River' for dataset 1 whereas Table 1 and Tables 4-5 use 'Liver' (p.9); kept as printed, treated as same dataset
Table 3/4 images: Vehicle1 and Dermatology CBHSID values lack bold; std formatting 'Yeast6 Cluster-C 0.8328' etc. read visually at 170 dpi (p.9)
best_other_* computed by me only as the max of printed values among the other six columns for convenience; not a winner decision
Abstract says G-Mean/Recall/F1 14 of 16 but text p.9 says recall and F1 12 of 16 and G-mean 10/12 binary + 3/4 multi (13); inconsistent claims within paper (p.1, p.9, p.13)
Table 2 labels ClusterCentroid as 'cluster based oversampling' (p.8), though it is an undersampler; printed as is
Table 5 (F1) and Table 6 not read in image form; not needed for chosen metric
notes: Datasets drawn from UCI and KEEL (text p.8); per-dataset repository, sizes and class counts not printed; Table 1 only has features, classes, IR. Imbalance ratio range text says 1.38 to 41.4. Multi-class IR 1.95 etc. as printed. Class thresholding: mean class size mu=Z_D/C_D; CBHSID resamples all classes to about mu (Eq.1, p.4) so for multiclass it undersamples/oversamples every class. Other metrics reported: Recall (Table 4, p.9), F1 (Table 5, p.10). Supplementary file not referenced. No GitHub link printed. Dataset-level results marked as image tables (Tables 1,3,4 rendered visually).
